title: Scaling Generate–Verify–Repair to Heterogeneous Multi‑Vendor NetOps Configurations (Repaired Preregistration)
research_question: Does a verifier-grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop significantly reduce operationally detectable policy-violation errors produced by a hosted-LLM when generating network configurations for operator intents across heterogeneous multi-vendor template families and topology patterns in a Mininet-based emulation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A GVR loop that uses deterministic syntax, reachability, and ACL verifiers will reduce the per-intent operational policy-violation rate (paired comparison) relative to single-call LLM generation.
GVR will reduce syntactic and topology-errors (mechanically verifiable) relative to LLM-only generation.
Relative improvement from GVR will vary across vendor/template families, with larger absolute reductions in vendor/template groups that show higher baseline error rates.
exploratory_questions: How many additional model calls (mean) does GVR use per avoided policy violation (cost tradeoff)?
What categories of semantic/policy violations remain after GVR and which verifier classes (syntax/reachability/ACL) most commonly fail to detect them?
benchmark_scope: Paired, provenance-traced intent→configuration workloads executed in Mininet emulation with synthetic vendor-specific configuration templates (3 vendor template families) and 4 topology patterns.
Scope explicitly bounded to the Mininet-emulated templates and the included template variability perturbations (no claims about production hardware generalization).
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: difference in the probability that an intent produces zero operationally-detectable policy violations under guarded (GVR) relative to baseline (LLM-only), measured over N paired intents.
secondary_estimands: Absolute and relative reduction in syntactic-error incidence (per-intent)
Absolute and relative reduction in topology (reachability) error incidence (per-intent)
Mean extra model calls per intent for guarded vs baseline
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired sample of N = 200 unique operator intents (paired episodes: baseline and guarded per intent). Stratified sampling across 3 vendor-template families and 4 topology patterns (12 strata) using the adapter's deterministic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index profile. Task_count is fixed at 200 and task_indices are selected deterministically by the adapter's task_index_profile prior to any model calls. Episodes_per_task = 2 (baseline, guarded). Initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Selection is fixed before observing model outputs and must not be changed based on outcomes.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: 10 percentage point absolute reduction (e.g., baseline 20% → guarded 10%), two-sided α=0.05, power=0.80. McNemar discordant-pair approximation yields required n≈157; N=200 chosen to provide margin and permit stratified subgroup description. With N=200 detectable absolute risk difference ≈8pp under same assumptions. Sensitivity analyses: recompute under baseline rates 10% and 30% and alternative discordant distributions; report bootstrap 95% CIs for risk difference.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any task flagged as duplicate by deterministic prompt+context hash comparison from the primary confirmatory analysis; duplicates will be reported and included in sensitivity analyses.

Exclude pairs aborted due to mapping_validation unit-test failures or CI-container template substitution failures from the primary paired test; these aborted pairs will be reported and included in sensitivity analyses.
Exclude pairs where automated audit/CI prevents execution due to environment integrity failures; such exclusions are logged and reported.
missingness_plan: Treat infrastructure/API failures and adapter errors as missing-at-random for the primary analysis under the 'complete_pair_primary' default. Pre-registered sensitivity analysis ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') will treat failed or partial pairs conservatively as failures (no-success). All failed calls, retries, and technical restarts will be logged; any pair with unrecoverable infrastructure failure will be excluded from the primary paired test and included in sensitivity reports.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of binary per-intent policy-violation presence (yes/no) using McNemar's test as implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (analysis_executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1). Report risk difference (guarded minus baseline) with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals (bootstrap performed on paired outcomes). Adhere to the analysis contract's failed-call treatment default 'complete_pair_primary' for primary inference and report sensitivity using 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Secondary analyses: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test for counts of syntax/topology errors (exploratory). Per-vendor subgroup effect-size summaries are descriptive and exploratory. Report mean additional model calls per avoided violation with 95% bootstrap CI. Record analysis code, exact bootstrap seeds, and runtime metadata.
multiplicity_plan: One predeclared primary estimand (policy-violation paired difference). Secondary estimands (syntax/topology reductions, cost) are exploratory and will be reported without alpha-adjusted confirmatory claims; p-values for secondary tests will be labeled exploratory and effect sizes with CIs provided.

stopping_rule: Stop after execution of all predeclared task_indices (N=200) and their paired episodes, or immediately if the maximum_model_calls budget (400) is exhausted, or if wall-clock execution exceeds the capability manifest limit of 7 days. Technical restarts permitted only per adapter policy and only for infrastructure recovery; unrecoverable infra failures exclude affected pairs as described in the missingness_plan and are logged.
